question: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 7 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \text{adj}(A)$, verify whether $AB = BA$.
explanation:
First compute $B = \text{adj}(A)$.

For $A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 7\end{bmatrix}$.

Cofactor matrix is $\begin{bmatrix}7 & -2 \\ -3 & 1\end{bmatrix}$.

Taking transpose gives $B = \begin{bmatrix}7 & -3 \\ -2 & 1\end{bmatrix}$.

Compute $AB$.

$AB = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 7\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}7 & -3 \\ -2 & 1\end{bmatrix}$.

$= \begin{bmatrix}7-6 & -3+3 \\ 14-14 & -6+7\end{bmatrix}$.

$= \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$.

Compute $BA$.

$BA = \begin{bmatrix}7 & -3 \\ -2 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 7\end{bmatrix}$.

$= \begin{bmatrix}7-6 & 21-21 \\ -2+2 & -6+7\end{bmatrix}$.

$= \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$.

Thus $AB = BA = I$.

options.B: $AB=BA=0$, so both products are zero matrices.
options.C: $AB\ne BA$ because matrix multiplication is never commutative.
